A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EchoFoley/EchoVidia work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The appendix sections can be matched despite renumbering and relocation of the impact discussion.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation benchmarks, human evaluations, sounding-event detection and localization results, and slow–fast ablations in Tables 2–3 and Figures 4–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark, human-evaluation, event-awareness, and ablation results.

M1.justification: The symbolic event representation, slow–fast reasoning, 12-action agent framework, event editing, synthesis, and mixing procedures are unchanged. The detailed prompts and base models also match across the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions use EchoFoley-6k derived from VGGSound and the PE Video Dataset, with the same 14 topics and generation, detection, and localization tasks. Revised dataset counts do not establish new domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same eight generation baselines, including four MMAudio configurations, ThinkSound, AudioGenie, and two HunyuanVideo-Foley configurations. The event-awareness comparators in Table 3 and Figure 6 are also unchanged; added related-work citations are not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 1 revises the reported benchmark pool from 500 to 937 videos and from 6,000 to 6,018 instructions. The stated evaluation samples, metrics, and procedures remain unchanged, including 100 generation cases, 50 human-evaluation pairs, and 300 awareness videos in Section 5.3. The PDFs do not establish rerunning the experiments.

E4.justification: The control-granularity analysis in Figure 5 and slow–fast ablations in Table 3 and Figure 6 are retained unchanged. No additional robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, or locally presented case studies appear.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run averaging for event awareness, the same Figure 6 error bars, and human inter-annotator agreement of 0.62 using Cohen’s kappa. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Descriptive dataset statistics change in Table 1: total sounding events increase from 3,612 to 5,622, while mean events per video changes from 7.2 to 6. Performance values and plotted findings in Tables 2–3 and Figures 4–6 are unchanged; no new performance improvement is reported.

T1.justification: The event-tuple and task definitions, controllability equations, and appendix metric pseudocode are unchanged. Neither version adds distinct theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same task, benchmark, and framework contributions. The headline claims of 40.7% better controllability and 12.5% better perceptual quality are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning visual dominance, control granularity, and slow–fast reasoning remain unchanged. The impact discussion moves from Section 6.3 to Appendix A without substantive revision, and the latency, VideoLLM-awareness, and diffusion-bias limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Both appendices disclose the same prompts, preprocessing, model configurations, hardware, and inference times. The project link and access information are unchanged; no additional implementation or reproducibility detail accompanies the revised dataset counts.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Video-to-audio generation with hidden alignment and Long-video audio synthesis with multi-agent collaboration. The overall positioning remains unchanged. The added published FoleyCrafter entry corresponds to an already-cited work, rather than a new research comparison.

P1.justification: The impact section moves into the appendix, shifting appendix letters. v2 also updates author affiliations, adds a corresponding-author note and funding acknowledgments, repairs references, and changes DepthCtl to VolCtl in Section 6.2. Most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: All eight figures and five tables retain their designs and membership. Front-matter edits and the relocated impact discussion reflow the pages, shifting appendix displays and increasing spacing around some metric explanations and pseudocode blocks.

improvement.justification: Small citation and terminology improvements are outweighed by a new inconsistency in benchmark reporting. Table 1 previously paired 500 videos and 6,000 instructions consistently with 12 instructions per video; v2 reports 937 videos and 6,018 instructions but retains 12, rather than approximately 6.42. This reduces reporting reliability without adding experimental validation, while the method and performance evidence remain unchanged.
